newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares hit all-time high, then lose momentum.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares hit all-time high, then lose momentum.

text.p: Greek shares consolidated on Tuesday, finishing 0.79 percent off after a firm opening which saw the benchmark index ground its way to new all-time highs.
The market looked set for consolidation having discounted good 1997 macroeconomic and corporate news, awaiting further progress in the economy.
"A large number of stocks has approached full valuation of macroeconomic input and expectations of upbeat 1997 corporate results," said Alexandros Sarrigeorgiou, fund manager at Allianz mutual funds.
Stocks should stay rangebound in the 1,700-1,800 band as long as telecom OTE's part-flotation and share capital increase are in the cards, he added.
"The market will hover between 1,700 and 1,800 points for as long as the part-flotation and share capital increase of OTE is at play," said another fund manager.
Tuesday's downturn did not affect sentiment and was seen as a normal profit-taking move.
"There is no broader concern because the underlying political and economic environment is positive, stable and reliable upon," said Sarrigeorgiou.
It should not come as surprise to anyone that some investors are tempted to realise their profits, he added.
"The correction may extend into Wednesday's session, but this will not unnerve investors," said another fund manager.
The Athens general index lost 0.79 percent or 13.65 points to 1,714.05 from Friday's 1,727.70.
It fluctuated between an all-time high of 1,755.66 and a low of 1,707.54.
All sector indices except for closed-end funds dipped on Tuesday.
Banks and industrials were off 0.16 and 0.64 percent, respectively.
Shares of new listing Xiosbank closed up 20 percent at 3,180 drachmas from its listing price of 2,650. There was open buy interest for 101,000 shares at close.
Monday's session was called off by the Athens stock exchange due to technical problems related to large buying interest for shares of new listing Xiosbank.
Greece's capital market commission imposed a 20 percent price volatility limit for Xiosbank to avoid system overloads stemming from wide price fluctuations in the stock.
The capital market commission had removed price volatility limits for the first three trading session in new listings on the Athens bourse.

Turnover soared to 43.4 billion drachmas in volume of 7.8 million shares, helped by sizeable put-through orders executed in National Housing Bank preferred, 270,000 shares at 9,850-9,900, and NIBID, 100,000 shares at 18,900-18,995.
Blocks were also traded in several banking issues, including National, Alpha Credit and Piraeus.
Declining stocks led advancers 150 to 82 with 24 stocks unchanged on 256 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,106-1,136. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were down 245 drachmas to 6,850.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted lower at 724.33-770.56. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $97.73-$99.42. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted lower at 4,113-4,346 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted lower at $24.27-$25.97. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted lower at 317-351 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
